transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Thank you so much for seeing me... I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not wasting your time, but my supervisor at the plant actually suggested I come in. 

It's... well, I guess I've been having a little trouble staying at my station on the production line. It's nothing malicious, I promise! It's just... I keep sort of popping up and leaving my spot when I'm supposed to stay put, even during our shift meetings. I just kind of take off before I even think about it. My supervisor said it's becoming a bit of a safety problem, which I feel really terrible about because I really want to be a good worker and follow the rules. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it okay.

Can you tell me whether you've noticed this kind of restlessness and difficulty staying in one place going back to when you were a child, or is this something that's only started more recently as an adult?

Um, well... I guess it's actually not a new thing. I feel a little embarrassed admitting it, but yeah, it goes back a really long way. 

Even back in elementary school, I was sort of... well, I was the kid who just couldn't seem to stay in my seat. I really wasn't trying to be a bad kid or anything, I promise! I just... I'd accidentally talk over the teacher, or my parents would get these notes sent home because I kept blurting things out or wandering around the classroom when we were supposed to be doing our work. I think I was just a really, really eager kid, you know? I always wanted to be helpful, my body just sort of moved faster than my brain. 

I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for... is that what you meant by going back to when I was a child?
Aside from the restlessness, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks or conversations, or notice yourself losing track of details, forgetting things, or getting easily distracted?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I hope it's okay to say no to that one! I actually feel like I'm pretty good at paying attention, especially when someone is talking to me. I really try hard to be a good listener, I promise. 

And at work, I don't really lose track of the details or forget what I'm supposed to be doing. My hands know exactly how to do the work on the line, and I can focus on it just fine. It's really just the... the staying put part that gets me in trouble, you know? My brain is focused on the job, it's just my body that wants to wander off. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting out answers before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in lines or discussions?

Um, well... I guess I do sometimes do that, yeah. I really, really try not to, though! I just... sometimes I'm so eager to help or be part of the team that I accidentally cut in on people without meaning to. 

Like, if my coworkers are talking, I might just sort of jump in because I think I have something helpful to add. Or if the line lead is asking a question, I'll sometimes blurt out the answer before they're even done talking. I just want to show that I know what to do, you know? But then... well, I can tell everybody gets a little irritated with me. I always apologize right away, though, I promise! I don't mean to be rude or anything. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a terrible coworker. I really do try to be polite!
Outside of work, do you notice this same restlessness or trouble staying seated—like at home, during meals, watching TV, or in social situations?

Um... outside of work? I haven't really noticed it being a problem, no. I hope that's okay to say! 

When I'm at home, I just like to keep busy, you know? Like doing chores or tidying up while the TV is on, just trying to be helpful around the house. So I'm not really trying to sit still for very long anyway. And with meals, I usually just grab something quick so I'm not in anyone's way or making a big fuss. 

I really try to just go with the flow when I'm around my friends or my family, so I don't think I'm restless or anything bad like that. I just like being active and pitching in. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right information... I'm really trying to answer everything as best as I can.
Have you ever had trouble sitting through things like a movie, a long meeting, a religious service, or a family gathering where you were expected to stay seated for a while?

Um, well... I guess I do have a little trouble with those sometimes. I mean, I really try to sit still and be respectful, especially for important things! But, um... if I have to sit through, like, a certification class at work or one of those long safety meetings, I just... I kind of get the wiggles, I guess? 

Like, my foot will start bouncing, or I'll catch myself clicking a pen over and over, or picking at my sleeves. I try to be quiet about it, but I end up shifting around in my chair a lot. Sometimes people actually ask me to stop because it's distracting them, which makes me feel awful. I really don't mean to bother anyone, I promise! It's just hard to keep my body completely still for that long. 

Is that... is that bad? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm not taking the meetings seriously. I really do listen to everything they say!
Have your family members or friends ever mentioned that your restlessness or blurting things out causes friction or problems in your relationships with them?

Um, with my family and friends... they're usually pretty understanding, I think. They just know I have a lot of energy and want to help. But... um... I guess where it really causes the most friction is actually at work. 

I'm really embarrassed to even admit this, and I really hope you don't think I'm a bad employee! I try so, so hard to do a good job. But... well, my supervisors have actually written me up recently. They said there were some safety and production problems because of me jumping in or moving around too much. It's gotten to the point where it's actually putting my job and my plans to get my new certifications at risk. 

And, um... I've noticed that my coworkers are a lot less willing to partner with me during shift handoffs now. I think I just overwhelm them or mess up their flow, even though I'm just trying to be eager and get things done fast for them! I hate knowing that I'm frustrating people. I really want to be someone they can rely on, you know? 

Does that... does that make sense? I'm so sorry, I know you asked about my friends, but the work stuff is just what's really scaring me right now. I hope it's okay that I shared that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a lifelong (since elementary school) pattern of hyperactive-impulsive symptoms—leaving her seat/station inappropriately, blurting out answers, interrupting others, fidgeting, and difficulty remaining seated during meetings—without significant inattentive symptoms (she denies distractibility, forgetfulness, or difficulty focusing on tasks).
